mainTopic: A father who forbids his property to his son but wants a future scholarly grandson to inherit: does 'קני על מנת להקנות' (acquire in order to pass it on) work?
overview: A man forbade his possessions to his son, who stole flax. He said that if his grandson became a תלמיד חכם, the son should acquire the property and then pass it to the grandson. The פומבדיתאי say this fails, because 'acquire in order to transfer' does not acquire. רב נחמן says it works, and he proves it from קנין סודר. רב אשי rejects that proof for two reasons: the cloth may really be acquired, and a סודר takes effect right away, while here the transfer only happens much later. רבא challenges רב נחמן from the בית חורון gift in the משנה, which did not work. רב נחמן answers that the meal showed the gift was not real, or that the משנה follows רבי אליעזר's strict view. The גמרא then asks whether the word 'כל' in the משנה includes the father's case. It answers that 'כל' includes רבא's later version instead, and the chapter השותפין ends with the הדרן.

steps.title: The story of the father, the thieving son, and the future scholar grandson
steps.stepSummary: A father forbids his property to his thieving son. When asked about a future scholarly grandson, he says the son should acquire it and then pass it to the grandson.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man whose son used to steal bundles of flax. The father made a vow forbidding his property to his son. People asked him: 'What if your grandson becomes a Torah scholar?' He answered: 'Let this son of mine acquire it, and if my grandson becomes a scholar, let the grandson acquire it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life case and lays out the father's exact words. It is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father does not want his son to benefit, but he also does not want to cut off a scholarly grandson. So he sets up a plan where the property goes through the son to the grandson. The question will be whether that plan can legally work.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who had a son
who used to snatch bundles of flax.
He forbade his possessions to him.
They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי הֲוַאי בַּר בְּרָךְ צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן, מַאי?
phrases.english: And if your grandson becomes a Torah scholar, what then?
He said to them: Let this one acquire,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the son, the one he just forbade.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי הֲוַאי בַּר בְּרִי צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: and if my grandson becomes a Torah scholar,
let him acquire them.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out the case: property goes to the son, but only so that a future scholarly grandson can acquire it.

steps.title: What is the law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the father's arrangement works.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a one-word question: does this plan actually work? The answers come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real question is whether the son, who is forbidden to benefit, can be a pipeline that passes the property on. If the son never truly owns it, can it still reach the grandson through him?

phrases.english: What is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the ruling on the case just described.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the property transfer under the father's arrangement, given that the son only gets it in order to pass it on?

steps.title: The פומבדיתאי: it does not work
steps.stepSummary: The פומבדיתאי say this is 'acquire in order to pass on,' and that kind of transfer does not take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פומבדיתאי say: this is a case of 'acquire in order to transfer,' and anything given as 'acquire in order to transfer' is not acquired.
steps.whatsHappening: The פומבדיתאי answer the question: the arrangement fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their point is that the son was never really meant to own anything. He was only a channel to the grandson. A person who gets something only to hand it on does not truly acquire it, so nothing passes through him.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sages of the city פומבדיתא
acquire on condition that you transfer it to someone else

phrases.english: The Sages of Pumbedita say:
It is "acquire in order to transfer,"
and any "acquire in order to transfer"
does not acquire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The transfer is void, because 'acquire in order to transfer' is not a real acquisition.

steps.title: רב נחמן: it does work, just like a cloth
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן disagrees and says the son does acquire, proving it from קנין סודר, where the cloth is also handed over only to make a deal happen.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב נחמן said: he does acquire. After all, the cloth used in a קנין סודר is a case of 'acquire in order to transfer,' and it works.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן argues with the פומבדיתאי and says the arrangement works. He brings a proof from the familiar קנין סודר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a קנין סודר, one person hands another a cloth to close a deal on something else. The cloth itself is not really meant to change owners, yet the deal still works. So 'acquire in order to transfer' can be effective, and here too the property can pass through the son to the grandson.

keyTerms.meaning: a cloth, used in קנין סודר (a symbolic act of acquisition)

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the passage is about whether קנין סודר really supports רב נחמן.

phrases.english: But Rav Nachman said: He acquires,
for after all, a cloth
phrases.notes: This is the cloth used in קנין סודר, handed over to close a deal on something else.

phrases.english: is "acquiring in order to transfer."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, opposing answer to the question in step 2, disagreeing with the פומבדיתאי and supporting his view from קנין סודר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Acquire in order to transfer' does work, so the arrangement is valid.
steps.raayaObject: That 'acquire in order to transfer' is effective.
steps.raayaSupportSource: קנין סודר, which works even though the cloth is given only to make the deal happen.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The transfer works, because 'acquire in order to transfer' is effective, as seen from קנין סודר.

steps.title: רב אשי: maybe the cloth really is acquired
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי questions the proof: who says the person receiving the cloth couldn't keep it if he grabbed it?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: And who tells us that if the receiver grabbed the cloth and held on to it, he would not get to keep it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי begins to knock down רב נחמן's proof from the cloth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן assumed the cloth is not truly acquired. רב אשי says maybe it is: the receiver usually just gives it back, but if he chose to keep it, perhaps it would be his. If so, the cloth is a real acquisition and does not prove anything about our case.

keyTerms.meaning: and who will tell us? (who says?)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
And who tells us that the cloth,
if he grabs it, it would not be held?
phrases.notes: He means: if the receiver grabbed the cloth to keep it, maybe it would really be his.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: וּמַאן לֵימָא לַן
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from סודר, not the question itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The cloth may be truly acquired by the receiver, so it is not a case of 'acquire only to transfer.'

steps.title: רב אשי's second point: a cloth works right away, but here the transfer comes much later
steps.stepSummary: Even if a סודר is 'acquire in order to transfer,' it acquires immediately. Here the son would only acquire when the grandson becomes a scholar, and by then the cloth has long been returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: a cloth is 'acquire in order to transfer, and acquire from now.' But these possessions of this man, when does the son acquire them? Only when his grandson becomes a Torah scholar. And by the time that happens, the cloth has already gone back to its owner!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second reason the cloth proof fails: the timing is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a סודר, the deal takes effect the moment the cloth is handed over. Here the son only acquires when the grandson becomes a scholar, maybe years later. By then the act of acquiring is long over, like a cloth already given back, so it cannot make the transfer happen.

keyTerms.meaning: the cloth has returned to its owner

steps.whatToRemember: The פומבדיתאי say 'acquire in order to transfer' does not work. רב נחמן says it does, based on סודר. רב אשי rejects the proof: the cloth may be truly acquired, and a סודר takes effect right away, while here the transfer only happens in the future.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying קנין סודר doesn't work. He is saying it is different from our case, so it cannot serve as a proof.

phrases.english: And furthermore:
"a cloth acquires in order to transfer
and acquires from now."
These possessions of this man,
when does he acquire?
phrases.notes: "He" is the son, who is supposed to pass the property to the grandson.

phrases.aramaic: לְכִי הָוֵי בַּר בְּרֵיהּ צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: When his grandson becomes a Torah scholar;
and when he becomes one,
the cloth has gone back to its owner!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד: סוּדָרָא קָנֵי עַל מְנָת לְהַקְנוֹת וְקָנֵי מִן הַשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second rejection of רב נחמן's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between סודר and the father's arrangement.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A סודר takes effect immediately, while here the acquisition would only happen in the future, after the act of acquiring is already finished.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב נחמן from the gift of בית חורון
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that the gift in the משנה of בית חורון was 'acquire in order to transfer,' and it did not take effect, which contradicts רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: But the gift of בית חורון is a case of 'acquire in order to transfer,' and there the person does not acquire!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's claim that 'acquire in order to transfer' really works. He brings a case straight from the משנה where it did not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the בית חורון case, the man gave his courtyard and meal to a friend only so that his own father, who was vowed from benefit, could come and eat. The חכמים said that gift does not count. So it seems 'acquire in order to transfer' fails, against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: The gift made in בית חורון, the case in the משנה on 48a
Acquire in order to transfer: you get it only so you can pass it on

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
But the gift of Beit Choron
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's case: a man gave his courtyard and meal to a friend so his vowed father could eat.

phrases.english: is a case of "acquire in order to transfer,"
and he does not acquire!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: וְהָא מַתְּנַת בֵּית חוֹרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב נחמן's main claim from step 4 and attacks it from the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule that 'acquire in order to transfer' takes effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's בית חורון gift is exactly this kind of transfer, and the חכמים ruled it is not a gift

steps.title: רב נחמן gives two answers
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers in two ways: either the meal itself shows the gift was not real, or the משנה follows רבי אליעזר's strict view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes he answered: It is because his meal proves about him. And sometimes he answered: That is רבי אליעזר's view, who said that even something people normally waive is forbidden to someone vowed from benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his view against רבא. He explains why the בית חורון gift failed without admitting that 'acquire in order to transfer' never works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Answer one: the problem was special to that case, since the fancy meal for his son's wedding showed he never really meant to hand it over. Answer two: the משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who is strict even about tiny waived benefits, so he is also strict here. Either way, the general rule of רב נחמן stays standing.

keyTerms.meaning: His meal proves about him, showing his real intention
Something so small that people normally let it go
Someone forbidden by a vow from getting benefit from another

steps.confusionAlert: These are two separate answers, not one. רב נחמן gave one answer at one time and the other answer at another time.

phrases.english: Sometimes he said to him:
It is because his meal proves about him,
phrases.notes: A big wedding meal for his own son shows he never truly meant to give it away.

phrases.english: and sometimes he said to him
that it is the view of Rabbi Eliezer,
who said: even something normally waived
is forbidden to one vowed from benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: זִימְנִין אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִשּׁוּם דִּסְעוּדָתוֹ מוֹכַחַת עָלָיו
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two answers: limit the משנה to its special facts, or assign it to a minority strict opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בית חורון case shows 'acquire in order to transfer' never works
steps.terutzMaskana: The case failed either because the meal showed the gift was fake, or because it follows רבי אליעזר's strictness

steps.title: Trying to prove from the word 'Any' in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule and asks what the word 'כל' adds, suggesting it adds the father's case and shows that his gift fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: The חכמים said: Any gift that is not such that if he consecrated it, it would be consecrated, is not a gift. What does 'any' come to include? Doesn't it include this case we have been discussing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה's general rule and asks what the extra word 'כל' adds. It suggests that it adds the father's arrangement, which would mean his gift does not work, against רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gift only counts if the receiver owns it fully, so fully he could even make it הקדש. The word 'כל' seems to widen the rule to more cases. If it widens it to the father's case, then the father's arrangement fails, which challenges רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: He made it holy, dedicated it to the בית המקדש
To include what? (asking what an extra word adds)

phrases.english: We learned: The Sages said:
Any gift that is not such
that if he consecrated it, it would be consecrated —
is not a gift.
"Any" comes to include what?
Is it not to include this matter
that was cast upon the sheaves?
phrases.notes: This points back to the father's case we've been discussing; the suggestion is that his gift does not work.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״כׇּל״ לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מַאי? לָאו לְאֵתוֹיֵי הָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב נחמן survives רבא's challenge, the גמרא tries a new attack from the wording of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that the son acquires in the father's arrangement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra word 'כל' must add some case, and the most likely one is the father's arrangement, which would then not be a gift

steps.title: No, 'Any' includes רבא's later version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof: 'כל' comes to include the later version of רבא's teaching, not the father's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it comes to include the later version of רבא's teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the attempted proof. 'כל' has a different job, so the father's case is not proven to fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's later version said that a gift made to get around a vow fails even if the giver only mentions the purpose casually, without making it a real condition. 'כל' adds that case. So the משנה says nothing against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: The later version of a teaching

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's view survives both attacks: רבא's challenge from בית חורון is answered, and the word 'כל' is explained as adding רבא's later version, not the father's case.

phrases.english: No,
it is to include the latter version
phrases.notes: רבא taught this on the daf earlier: the gift fails even if the purpose is only mentioned casually.

phrases.english: of Rava's teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְאֵתוֹיֵי לִישָּׁנָא בָּתְרָאָה דִּשְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof suggested in step 9
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reading that 'כל' includes the father's case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'כל' can be explained as adding another case, רבא's later version, so it does not prove anything about the father's arrangement

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the chapter השותפין
steps.stepSummary: The chapter הַשּׁוּתָּפִין ends with the traditional closing line.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter הַשּׁוּתָּפִין.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing formula marking the end of the chapter. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is said at the end of every chapter, showing our wish to come back and learn it again. The discussion of 'acquire in order to transfer' ends here.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the closing words for a finished chapter
The partners: the name of this chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, HaShutafin

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion
